lineItems.name: On-Peak (4pm-9pm)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost to deliver power during the most expensive time of day, 4 PM to 9 PM.

lineItems.name: Off-Peak
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost to deliver power during standard hours when demand is lower.

lineItems.name: Super Off-Peak
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost to deliver power during the cheapest hours, usually late at night or early morning.

lineItems.name: Base Services Charge
lineItems.plainEnglish: A fixed monthly fee that covers the basic costs of maintaining the grid, like your meter and power lines.

lineItems.name: Baseline Adjustment Credit
lineItems.plainEnglish: A discount for staying within a basic amount of energy usage for your area.

lineItems.name: SDG&E Electric Generation (390 kWh)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost of the electricity itself, which is then canceled out by the credit below.

lineItems.name: SDG&E Generation Credit
lineItems.plainEnglish: This credit removes the SDG&E generation charge because you are buying your power from San Diego Community Power instead.

lineItems.name: San Diego Community Power - PowerOn (390 kWh)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the actual cost for the electricity you used, provided by San Diego Community Power.

lineItems.name: Power Charge Indifference Adjustment (PCIA)
lineItems.plainEnglish: A fee to cover costs for older power contracts that SDG&E signed before you switched to a community provider.

lineItems.name: Wildfire Fund Charge
lineItems.plainEnglish: A state-mandated fee that helps pay for wildfire safety and liability costs.

lineItems.name: State Regulatory Fees & Franchise Fees
lineItems.plainEnglish: Fees paid to the state and local government for the right to operate and provide energy services.

lineItems.name: Electric Users Tax
lineItems.plainEnglish: A tax collected by SDG&E on behalf of your local city government.

analysis.summary: Your bill reflects a total usage of 390 kWh, with about 16% of that energy consumed during the expensive 4-9 PM peak window. Your costs are driven by a mix of delivery fees, the generation cost from San Diego Community Power, and standard state taxes.
analysis.topSavingTip: Since you used 62 kWh during the 4-9 PM peak window, try shifting heavy appliance use like laundry or dishwashing to the Super Off-Peak hours to lower your delivery costs.

lineItems.name: Gas Service
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost for the natural gas you used during this billing period.

lineItems.name: Gas Energy Charge (31 of 32 Days)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a portion of your gas usage charge based on the rate active for most of the month.

lineItems.name: Gas Energy Charge (1 of 32 Days)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a portion of your gas usage charge based on a rate change that occurred for the final day.

lineItems.name: California Climate Credit (Gas)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a state-mandated credit to help lower your energy costs.

lineItems.name: Public Purpose Program (Gas)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This fee funds state-mandated energy efficiency and low-income assistance programs.

lineItems.name: State Regulatory Fee (Gas)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a small fee to cover the costs of state utility regulation.

lineItems.name: Electricity Delivery (31 Day Charge)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost for SDG&E to maintain the power lines and deliver electricity to your home.

lineItems.name: Electricity Delivery (1 Day Charge)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the delivery cost for the final day of your billing cycle.

lineItems.name: DWR Bond Charge
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a state charge to pay off bonds from the 2001 energy crisis.

lineItems.name: Electricity Generation (31 Day Charge)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost for the actual electricity you consumed.

lineItems.name: Electricity Generation (1 Day Charge)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is the cost for the electricity used on the final day of the cycle.

lineItems.name: DWR Revenue Adjustment
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a small adjustment related to state energy bond collections.

lineItems.name: Baseline Adjustment Credit
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a discount for staying within your baseline energy allowance.

lineItems.name: California Climate Credit (Electric)
lineItems.plainEnglish: This is a state-mandated credit to help lower your energy costs.

analysis.summary: Your bill was driven by 757 kWh of electricity usage and 45 therms of gas. About 24% of your electricity was used during the expensive 4-9 PM on-peak window.
analysis.topSavingTip: Since you are on a Time-of-Use plan, try to shift your heavy appliance use, like laundry or dishwashing, to before 4 PM or after 9 PM to avoid the highest rates.
